2023 global fishing activity

The Invisible Ocean | A. Spatial distribution

T01 Annual map    T02 FAO areas    T03 Concentration

111.71 million hours of estimated fishing activity across 1,193,301 active grid cells in 2023. Each grid covers 0.1° by 0.1° and can include activity from multiple vessels.

T01 · Annual grid map

plot of chunk map

The highest-hour grid was centred at 119.35<U+00B0> E, 35.05<U+00B0> N near the coast of eastern China, with 316,398.92 hours. The Northwest Pacific accounts for a large share of the global total, as the regional comparison below quantifies. Of the 2,040,786 grid cells recorded in the dataset, 847,485 had zero estimated fishing hours.

T02 · FAO marine area totals

plot of chunk areas

The Northwest Pacific (61) recorded 68.29 million hours, or 61.13% of the global total. The Northeast Atlantic (27) and Western Indian Ocean (51) followed with 9.01 and 6.79 million hours, respectively. The global denominator includes 2.34 million hours (2.09%) from grid centres outside the FAO marine polygons.

Ranking is based on annual hours, with ties ordered by grid_id. A cell is active if its annual hours are positive. Each cutoff rounds up to a whole grid, and the cumulative curve ends at 100%. Shares describe a percentage of active grid cells. The physical area of a 0.1° cell varies by latitude.

Sources and interpretation

Global Fishing Watch estimates apparent fishing activity from AIS observations. AIS reception and classification vary by location. Report the results as estimated hours in the observed data. The regional chart compares total hours and does not adjust for region size.
